MUST_FIX B-01 — P1, confidence0.96 — Specify race-safe OMP approval-to-tool-call correlation. Exact anchor: specs/epics/e05-thin-tool-integration/PLAN.md:76. ToolV1 requires permission.params.tool_call_id to be a genuine tool-call identifier (specs/contracts/tool-integration-v1.md:50-52). However, the proposed initialization/typed UI path reaches ExtensionUIContext.approve, whose prompt contains full/compact renderings and optional session/grants, but no toolCallId. The pinned requestApproval implementation constructs exactly that identifier-free object. The genuine ID is emitted separately by ExtensionToolWrapper in tool_approval_requested, while the agent loop supports concurrent tool execution. Source evidence: https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts#L260-L337 ; https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/approval.ts#L699-L736 ; https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/wrapper.ts#L385-L450 ; https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts#L3833-L3857 . Impact: The specified path does not establish the mandatory exact SDK-call-to-original-responder binding. A latest-event guess is unsafe for overlapping approvals, and a callback-generated surrogate is not the genuine ID required by the contract. This is an unresolved plan-level identity seam, not an allegation that nonexistent implementation already misroutes permissions. Minimal fix: Specify a concrete source-backed binding before Build, such as an adapter-owned inline tool_approval_requested handler and bounded serialized approval gate that retains that event's actual toolCallId through its corresponding approve promise and terminal disposition. Define cancellation/teardown behavior and require an offline overlapping-two-approval case proving each exact original ID/responder remains bound. Do not weaken the genuine-ID requirement or use prose/latest-event matching.

SHOULD_FIX B-02 — P2, confidence0.98 — Pin the adapter's approval policy instead of inheriting YOLO defaults. Exact anchor: specs/epics/e05-thin-tool-integration/PLAN.md:76-78. The plan specifies interactivePrompts, UI-context installation and once/deny rendering, but no effective tools.approvalMode or isolated per-tool policy. In the pinned SDK, tools.approvalMode defaults to yolo, which auto-approves every tier; resolveApprovalFromContext uses that configured default. Installing the approve/UI callback does not enable ordinary write/exec approval requests. Source evidence: https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/settings.ts#L294-L317 ; https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/packages/coding-agent/src/tools/approval.ts#L75-L106 ; https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/45c35e40c46166dc726ccc52f5d27f40f2449f99/docs/sdk.md . Impact: In the plan's private/default environment, normal write/exec work need not produce the genuine permission callbacks required by S04 allow/deny acceptance; it may execute under SDK policy without consulting the installed responder. Ambient per-tool allow overrides can also defeat an intended asking profile. This does not equate all tool-internal autonomous work with an amux authority bypass. Minimal fix: Specify adapter-owned isolated effective settings, for example always-ask with no inherited allow overrides for the exercised write/exec tools, and pass them into the one createAgentSession. Require an offline real-wrapper check that the selected operation reaches approve and denial prevents its effect. Preserve the explicit once/deny-only UI and separately approved real-provider gate.

No consider findings. The packet otherwise carefully preserves the shared authority/admission, original-responder, bounds, cleanup, ACP/native lifecycle and historical native-fence boundaries, and it distinguishes source feasibility, Plan approval, Build authorization and real runtime acceptance. These two concrete SDK-adapter planning gaps prevent the requested independent Plan PASS.
